lines.h1: Todoist or TickTick? Here's the answer in ten seconds.
lines.h2: Want the fastest way to get tasks out of your head, and a clean list? Todoist.
lines.h3: Want a timer, habits, a calendar and a priority matrix, all in one app? TickTick.
lines.h4: Now, five rounds to prove it. Plus one bonus round, where a third app comes in.
lines.r1a: Round one. Getting tasks out of your head.
lines.r1b: Todoist's Quick Add reads a plain sentence and sets the date, the repeat and the project. And Ramble lets you just talk.
lines.r1c: TickTick understands plain sentences too, and its AI Voice Add splits one spoken paragraph into separate tasks.
lines.r1d: It's close, but for pure speed, round to Todoist.
lines.r2b: TickTick gives you month, week and day calendars, with a Timeline, right next to your tasks.
lines.r2c: Todoist has a calendar layout too, but its strength is syncing with the calendar you already use.
lines.r2d: For time blindness, round to TickTick.
lines.r3a: Round three. Everything in one app.
lines.r3b: TickTick has a Pomodoro timer with white noise, a habit tracker and an Eisenhower priority matrix built in.
lines.r3c: Todoist stays a task list. For a timer or habits, you add another app.
lines.r4b: Todoist is clean, and it stays out of your way.
lines.r4c: TickTick's extra tools are one more thing to set up, and organizing can turn into a hobby.
lines.r4d: If options overwhelm you, round to Todoist.
lines.r5a: Round five. Works on every device.
lines.r5b: TickTick runs on iPhone, Android, Apple Watch, Mac, Windows, Linux and the web.
lines.r5c: Todoist covers the exact same list.
lines.sc: Two rounds each, and a tie. So don't pick the better app. Pick the one built for your problem.
lines.b1: One more round. The moment you freeze on a task you've been avoiding.
lines.b2: Both are great at organizing. But a better list doesn't make you start. Your list in Todoist, your list in TickTick.
lines.f1: Full disclosure, that's the gap we built FOCO for. It starts from the task you're putting off.
lines.f2: It breaks the task into tiny steps, each with a time estimate.
lines.f3: Then step one opens into a focus session, with a timer and a companion working next to you.
lines.o1: So. Todoist for fast capture and a clean list. TickTick for one app that holds everything.
lines.o2: And FOCO when the list is fine, but you still can't begin. Tell me in the comments which one you are.
